notes: Field elements are hex, big-endian here for readability; on the wire they are 32-byte little-endian. The scenario uses a test verifier that accepts exactly one 480-byte proof: "valid-proof" padded with zeros. eventsH is the byte string of SPEC-WIRE §6 whose SHA-256 enters the digest. rejected lists the envelopes an indexer must refuse; the reason is informative, only the refusal is normative.

sections.envelopes: Each envelope of the scenario: its bytes, and for a spend its bodyHash (SPEC-WIRE §4: SHA256("sh20/v0/body" ‖ body) mod r, body from "SH20" up to the proof).
sections.claim: One CLAIM: the message SHA256("sh20/v0/claim" ‖ listTxid ‖ npk) and its BIP340 signature by lockKey, with 32 zero bytes of auxiliary randomness.
sections.preActivation: digest_{A-1}: the digest an indexer starts from at block A.
sections.carriers: One transaction each, and what SPEC-WIRE §3 finds in it. expect is the hex of the one counted envelope, "none" when no envelope is counted (an envelope of another version alone is "none"), or "many" when two or more are counted (the transaction is refused). Inputs give their witness only; their outpoints play no part. {"coinbase": true} is the input of a coinbase.
sections.scenario.verifierCalls: Every call to the verifier, in order, with its nine public inputs in the order of SPEC-WIRE §4: R[anchorHeight], nf0, nf1, leaf0, leaf1, leaf2, bodyHash, vPub, tPub. The proof is checked last (§5), so a spend refused for another reason is not in the list. An anchor below A is checked against the empty root.
sections.scenario.after: For each block: root R[H], the event types, eventsH, and digest_H.
sections.scenario.blocks: The transactions of each block. vin[].prevHeight is the height of the block that confirmed the output an input spends, given where a DEPLOY needs it (SPEC-WIRE §5: its commit must be N = deployMaturity blocks old; here N = 3).

claim.note: BIP340 signature with 32 zero bytes of auxiliary randomness, by the key whose secret is SHA256("lock2-secret")

preActivation.note: Blocks below A have no root and no digest. digest_{A-1} = SHA256("sh20-v0"), whatever an indexer read before A.
